description.value: The study examined correlations between food-related problem behaviors and BOLD responses to visual food cues before and after eating in normal-weight and overweight/obese participants.

spans.text: In this study, functional magnetic resonance imaging and survey data were evaluated for correlations between food-related problem behaviors and the neural regions underlying responses to visual food cues before and after eating in normal-weight individuals and overweight/obese individuals.

value: we predicted food-related behavior will be positively correlated with neural activation in the striatum, OFC, DLPFC, insula, thalamus, hypothalamus, amygdala, and hippocampus in response to high-calorie food cues during hunger (premeal condition) in normal-weight and overweight/obese individuals.
After eating, we expected correlations between eating behaviors and neural reward response to food cues in overweight/obese individuals but not among normal-weight participants

name.value: FRPQ-SATIETY correlation with high-calorie food vs. object activation in normal-weight participants

definition.value: Activity in the left amygdala was positively correlated with FRPQ-SATIETY during the high-calorie vs. object contrast for the normal-weight group.

value: During the premeal scan, activity in the left amygdala was positively correlated with FRPQ-SATIETY during the high-calorie vs. object contrast for the normal-weight group.
Those with more satiety-related problems had greater activity in the amygdala in response to high-calorie food in contrast to objects.

name.value: FRPQ-SATIETY correlation with low-calorie food vs. object activation in overweight/obese participants

definition.value: Premeal activity in the right DLPFC was negatively correlated with FRPQ-SATIETY in the low-calorie vs. object contrast.

value: For the overweight/obese group, premeal activity in the right DLPFC was negatively correlated with FRPQ-SATIETY in the low-calorie vs. object contrast.
The DLPFC may be part of an inhibitory system that controls one's feeling of satiety; individuals scoring lower in satiety impairment preferentially activate this inhibitory system.

name.value: Postmeal FRPQ-SATIETY correlation with low-calorie food vs. object activation in the right putamen

definition.value: Activation in the putamen was positively correlated with FRPQ-SATIETY in the low vs. object condition after eating.

value: After eating, activation in the right putamen was positively correlated with FRPQ-SATIETY in the low-calorie vs. object condition among overweight/obese participants.

Those who report being less likely to be satiated after a normal-sized meal had greater activity in the putamen postmeal, suggesting that motivation to eat may still be present despite reporting very little hunger.
